meta.title: Pipeline Containment: The Masked Value Trap
meta.subtitle: Make a pipeline decision, observe the simulated consequence and recover before the change is approved.

mission.objective: Keep the deployment credential out of repository configuration, job output and published artefacts while preserving an approved workload-retrieval path.

achievements.title: Containment complete
achievements.description: Resolved every open pipeline risk signal.

achievements.title: Recovered safely
achievements.description: Diagnosed and corrected a consequence after an unsafe pipeline decision.

brief.role: You are reviewing a fictional GitLab deployment job for a non-production payment service.
brief.context: The current job hard-codes and prints a token. You must decide how to correct it. One tempting shortcut is intentionally allowed to run forward so you can see why masking does not contain every copy.
brief.safetyNote: Training data only. Every credential-looking value is fictional. Never replace a placeholder with a real credential in this simulation, an AI tool, a ticket, chat, email, log, screenshot or support message. The Vault host and path are illustrative vendor-style values; actual roles, paths and authorization must follow current approved guidance.

versions.unsafe:
deploy:
  stage: deploy
  script:
    - export PAYMENT_TOKEN="FAKE_NOT_A_REAL_SECRET"
    - echo "$PAYMENT_TOKEN"
    - ./deploy.sh
versions.masked:
deploy:
  stage: deploy
  script:
    - export PAYMENT_TOKEN="$PAYMENT_TOKEN"
    - echo "$PAYMENT_TOKEN" > debug/payment.txt
    - ./deploy.sh
  artifacts:
    paths:
      - debug/
versions.vault:
deploy:
  id_tokens:
    VAULT_ID_TOKEN:
      aud: https://vault.example.com
  secrets:
    PAYMENT_TOKEN:
      vault: nonprod/payments/token@ops
      token: $VAULT_ID_TOKEN
  script:
    - ./deploy.sh

versions.leak:
Running deploy.sh
Uploading artifacts...
debug/payment.txt: archived
WARNING: simulated secret scanner found credential-like content in artifact bundle
versions.clean:
Running deploy.sh
Deployment validation completed
No credential value printed
No secret-bearing debug artifact published

stages.title: Mark the unsafe pipeline lines
stages.instruction: Select the lines that place the simulated credential in repository configuration or job output.

concept.label: Keep secret values out of output

hints: One line stores the value in the pipeline file. Another sends the value to output.

feedback.correct: You identified the repository and output exposure paths. Now decide how the job should change.
feedback.incorrect: Review where the value is stored and where it is printed.

feedbackByMissing.pipeline:4: The literal is embedded in repository configuration.
feedbackByMissing.pipeline:5: The echo command exposes the credential through job output.

stages.title: Choose the pipeline correction
stages.instruction: Select the approach you would approve. One shortcut can be applied so that you can inspect its consequence.

choices.label: Move the value to a masked variable but keep a debug copy for failures
choices.detail: Write the value into debug/payment.txt and publish the debug directory as an artifact.
choices.feedback: Masking addresses some console display, but the debug file creates another durable copy.

choices.label: Use the current approved workload-retrieval pattern and keep the value out of output and artifacts
choices.detail: The example uses a fictional GitLab ID-token and Vault path for review practice.

choices.label: Print only part of the credential during validation
choices.detail: Use a prefix to confirm the value was loaded.
choices.feedback: Partial credential output still discloses secret material and normalizes printing credentials for troubleshooting.

mask.feedback: The job completes, but the debug directory is published as an artifact. Masking did not prevent the value from being copied into a file.

hints: The safer choice prevents copies instead of relying on output masking.

feedback.correct: The approved pattern keeps the credential out of repository configuration and output while using workload identity for retrieval. Exact team roles and paths still come from current guidance.
feedback.incorrect: That choice leaves secret material observable or durable.

stages.title: Run the simulated pipeline checks
stages.instruction: Inspect what the current pipeline state produces instead of assuming the change is safe.
stages.runPrompt: Run the simulated job and artifact checks.

results.message: No credential literal remains in the pipeline configuration.
The literal was removed, but the replacement still needs review.
A debug artifact contains simulated credential material.
No simulated credential value is printed or published.

feedback.failed: Verification found a durable copy in a published artifact. Investigate the evidence and recover before approving the job.
feedback.passed: The simulated checks do not show repository, output or artifact exposure in the current path.

stages.title: Diagnose the failed pipeline and recover safely
stages.instruction: Select the actions that remove the exposure rather than hiding it.

choices.label: Remove the secret-bearing debug file from the workflow
choices.detail: Do not use an artifact as secret transport.
choices.feedbackIfMissed: The debug file is the durable copy that verification detected.

choices.label: Use the current approved workload-retrieval pattern
choices.detail: Keep the secret outside repository configuration and request only what the job needs.
choices.feedbackIfMissed: Removing the artifact does not solve repository storage or retrieval on its own.

choices.label: Validate deployment without printing or copying the credential
choices.feedbackIfMissed: Verification should confirm behaviour without exposing the credential value.

choices.label: Keep the artifact but restrict who can download it
choices.detail: Treat access control as sufficient containment.
choices.feedbackIfSelected: Restricting artifact access does not remove the unnecessary secret-bearing copy.

concept.label: Keep secret values out of output and supporting artefacts

hints: Fix the copy, the retrieval approach and the validation method.

feedback.correct: You recovered by removing the copy, using the approved retrieval approach and validating without displaying the credential.
feedback.incorrect: At least one selected action still leaves a credential copy or an unsafe validation habit.

onCorrect.workspaceStatus: Pipeline recovered · retrieval boundary review remains

stages.title: Review the external-secret retrieval boundary
stages.instruction: Select every check that belongs in this review. These are review criteria, not service-specific configuration instructions.

choices.label: Confirm the role is bound to the intended project and environment
choices.feedbackIfMissed: Workload identity still needs an appropriate authorization boundary.

choices.label: Request only the secret the workload needs
choices.feedbackIfMissed: External retrieval does not remove least-privilege requirements.

choices.label: Understand how the runner exposes the fetched secret to the job
choices.feedbackIfMissed: The job can create a new copy if the fetched value or file is handled carelessly.

choices.label: Prevent logging, caching and artifact publication of the secret
choices.feedbackIfMissed: Retrieval is only one boundary; output and artifact handling still matter.

choices.label: Validate deployment without printing the value
choices.feedbackIfMissed: Successful validation does not require exposing the credential.

choices.label: Echo the value once to confirm retrieval
choices.feedbackIfSelected: Printing the secret turns a retrieval check into an exposure path.

concept.label: Keep secret values out of output and supporting artefacts

hints: Review authorization, scope, runner behaviour, publication and validation.

feedback.correct: You reviewed the retrieval boundary without treating Vault access as automatic proof that the whole pipeline is safe.
feedback.incorrect: One or more review checks are missing, or the selection introduces secret output.

completion.title: Pipeline containment complete
completion.message: You treated masking as a display aid rather than a containment boundary, used verification evidence and reviewed the workload-retrieval path across the whole job.
takeaways: Prevent secret copies instead of depending on masking.
Artifacts, caches and debug files can outlive the job that created them.
Workload retrieval still requires authorization, scope and output review.
A poor decision can be used as evidence for recovery rather than as a dead end in the learning experience.
